examples.name: Default
examples.description: A neutral status in the default subtle emphasis and md size.

examples.name: Law
examples.description: tone="law" says the item belongs to law (tone="wealth" for wealth), not a matter category.

examples.name: Bold
examples.description: emphasis="bold" is a solid fill for a label that has to stand out in a busy row; it doesn't change the meaning.

examples.name: Status tone
examples.description: information, warning, error, and success are statuses; the words carry the meaning and the tone's color supports it.

examples.name: Small, in a dense table
examples.description: size="sm" uses heading-xxs and less padding, for dense tables and compact cards.

examples.name: Qualifier after a Text Field's input
examples.description: A short, non-interactive unit or qualifier in Text Field's iconAfter slot.

antiExamples.name: A sentence in a Label
antiExamples.jsx: <Label tone="warning">Needs review before the filing deadline</Label>
antiExamples.reason: Label doesn't wrap and has no ellipsis, so in a narrow space a sentence runs past its container. Keep it to a status or a state in one to three words.

antiExamples.name: A category in a status tone
antiExamples.reason: Label's tones mean something, so a category in information blue reads as a status. Use Tag for a category or classification: <Tag tone="purple">Estate planning</Tag>.

antiExamples.name: A clickable Label
antiExamples.jsx: <Label tone="information" onClick={() => openTrust('averill-family')}>Averill Family Living Trust</Label>
antiExamples.reason: Label renders a span that isn't focusable, so keyboard users can't reach the click handler. Use Tag with href for a value that links to a record.

antiExamples.name: Label as a form control's name
antiExamples.reason: Label isn't a form label: it isn't tied to the control, so the field stays unnamed. Name a control with Field: <Field label="Matter name"><TextField /></Field>.
